title: Canary Watch Control Loop — Daily Rollup and Action Items
content:
Purpose:
Daily rollup from the Canary Watch control loop (rolling model rollout + infra signals). This doc captures timestamps, quick decisions, short diagnostics, and action items for follow-up. Intended for on-call rotation, release owners, and reliability leads.

Attendees:
- Riley Chen (owner)
- Marta Ruiz (SRE, metrics + alerts)
- Devon Patel (Serving runtime)
- Samir Kwon (Release eng)
- Elena Foster (Platform eng, autoscaler)
- Notes taken live in slack thread: #canary-watch

Context / short background:
- Canary started 2025-03-12 07:45 UTC for model v3.2 -> v3.3 incremental rollout at 5% traffic. Control loop configured to escalate at 2% user-facing error delta OR 50ms P99 latency increase over baseline.
- Canary window planned: 4 hours with automatic ramp to 20% if no escalation.
- Baseline = v3.2 in prod region-us-west with 99th latency 180ms and error rate 0.6%.

Timeline (timestamped events):
- 2025-03-12 07:45 UTC: Canary rollout start, 5% traffic, initial health checks green.
- 2025-03-12 08:12 UTC: Marta: alerted — HTTP 5xx rate increased from 0.6% -> 1.9% across canary hosts (signal: API.gateway.errors).
- 2025-03-12 08:18 UTC: Quick triage: increased tail latency on a subset of nodes (p95 -> p99 stretched), KV cache hit rate dropped on canary nodes (62% -> 49%).
- 2025-03-12 08:22 UTC: Decision: Pause ramp, pin canary to 5% and enable debug logging for model-io on canary group.
- 2025-03-12 08:32 UTC: Devon investigated model-io batching config mismatch — v3.3 uses dynamic microbatching default that in our environment resulted in backpressure during small request bursts.
- 2025-03-12 08:38 UTC: Hotfix (non-disruptive): adjust microbatching target from auto -> 8 token-window for canary group, restart 3/8 canary pods in rolling fashion.
- 2025-03-12 08:55 UTC: Post-hotfix metrics: 5xx rate fell to 0.9%, KV cache hit rate recovered to 68%. P99 latency dropped ~40ms vs peak.
- 2025-03-12 09:10 UTC: Canary resumed slow ramp to 10% after manual signoff.
- 2025-03-12 10:05 UTC: Observed small regression in generation quality (auto eval set BLEU-like metric down ~1.2%). Logged as a low-severity quality regression.
- 2025-03-12 11:45 UTC: Roll to 15% with monitoring window. No new errors, quality regression under threshold for now.
- 2025-03-12 12:15 UTC: Final decision to hold at 15% pending extended eval; release owner asked for 24h extended hold.

Immediate decisions taken:
- Pause automatic ramp at detection of 5xx > 2% and investigate before scaling.
- Apply microbatching override for v3.3 in current infra to mitigate backpressure (owner: Devon, applied 08:38 UTC).
- Keep canary pinned at 15% until extended automatic eval completes (owner: Samir).

Key diagnostics / root-cause notes:
- Primary cause of the spike: batching behavior mismatch -> small bursts caused internal queueing and KV cache churn. When microbatching aimed to aggregate tokens differently it increased memory pressure on a subset of nodes, causing cache eviction and higher tail latency.
- Secondary: autoscaler cooldown settings (scale-down aggressiveness) allowed node reclamation in the middle of the canary, amplifying cache misses.
- Not a model correctness bug: quality dip is minor and likely due to sampling variance after runtime changes (need more controlled eval).

Metrics snapshot (canary vs baseline, peak window):
- Error rate (5xx): baseline 0.6% -> canary peak 1.9% -> post-hotfix 0.9%
- P99 latency: baseline 180ms -> peak 260ms -> post-hotfix ~220ms
- KV cache hit rate: baseline 76% -> canary pre-fix 49% -> post-fix 68%
- Throughput (tokens/s per host): baseline 1.2k -> canary 1.0k during peak
- Cost signal: small bump due to retries (estimated +2.1% for the canary window)

Action items (owners and due dates):
- Devon: formalize microbatching override as a temporary compatibility shim and add to canary-runbook with command snippets. Due 2025-03-14.
- Elena: tune autoscaler cooldowns for canary pools (increase min node lifespan from 60s -> 180s) and run a small stress test. Due 2025-03-16.
- Marta: add a composite alert that considers KV cache hit delta + p99 latency to reduce false positives for noisy endpoints. Due 2025-03-18.
- Samir: schedule extended 24h evaluation window, coordinate with data-science to run the fixed evaluation harness on the logged requests and the automated prompt-set. Due 2025-03-13 (start).
- Riley: document the observed quality variance and link to evaluation artifacts + attach sample request IDs showing token-level diffs. Due 2025-03-15.
- Release owner (Samir): do not promote to 100% until evaluation passes threshold and infra mitigations are confirmed (safety hold). Ongoing.

Follow-ups / notes to self (informal):
- Consider adding a pre-warm traffic shim that sends a small steady-state traffic profile before increasing batch sizes — might reduce eviction windows.
- Investigate whether the runtime should expose a per-model microbatch target that persists across deploys (rather than relying on the runtime auto heuristics).
- We should capture a micro-origin trace (request->kv->model exec timeline) in the canary to reproduce the cache churn offline.

Risk register (short):
- If autoscaler change is delayed: potential recurring small outages during rolling deploys (low->medium risk).
- If microbatching persists unmitigated: risk of increased unit cost and user-visible latency regressions on long-tail traffic patterns (medium risk).
- Quality regression currently low severity, but needs repeated verification against holdout prompt-sets (monitoring).

Notes about changelog / release notes (what to include if promoted):
- Call out microbatching behavior change as "compatibility note" for infra teams.
- Mention that autoscaler cooldown was tuned to reduce cache churn during rollouts.
- Include pointer to evaluation results and metric deltas in the release notes.

Things to archive to Confluence and link from this doc:
- canary-runbook (confluence://runbooks/canary-watch) - steps and rollback commands
- RELENG-342 (jira) - tracking autoscaler tuning and postmortem
- PR: github.com/redwood/release-runner/pull/789 - microbatching override implementation

Unresolved questions:
- What threshold for KV cache delta should trigger an automated rollback vs. a pause? Current threshold (15% delta) seemed noisy; need a composite threshold.
- Do downstream customers see any correlated errors (CS reported a couple of tickets); need to correlate with user request IDs.

Quick wins identified:
- Short-term: persist microbatching override in the canary config to avoid repeated restarts.
- Mid-term: add a traffic pre-warm step to control initial burst distribution.

Appendix: sample quick command snippets (copied from runbook)
- Pause auto-roll: ./release-runner pause --canary-id=2025-03-12-rc3
- Apply override: kubectl patch deployment release-v3.3 -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"microbatch-target":"8"}}}}}'
- Roll restart 3 pods: kubectl rollout restart deployment/release-v3.3 --patch='{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"restartedAt":"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"}}}}}' --record

End of rollup. Will update after the extended evaluation completes and autoscaler tuning test runs.

Quick log pointer: slack thread #canary-watch started 2025-03-12 07:44 UTC (search: "canary v3.3 pause microbatch").

-- Riley
